  - Get stakeholder sign-off (owner: Product) — AC: email acceptances from Eng/Design/Data/CS.

2) Story: Design onboarding checklist & copy (3 pts)
- Description: Design modal/checklist UI and microcopy for treatment variant and small adjustments to control if needed.
- Subtasks:
  - Create high-fidelity mock (owner: Design)
  - Create responsive behavior & tooltip specs (owner: Design)
  - Accessibility review (owner: Design/QA)
- Acceptance criteria: Figma mocks approved; copy approved; design handoff ready.

3) Story: Frontend implementation (5–8 pts)
- Description: Implement modal/checklist & tooltips, integrate with experiment flagging, ensure responsive & accessible.
- Subtasks:
  - Implement UI components (owner: Frontend)
  - Hook to feature flagging system (owner: Frontend)
  - Event firing for displayed/completed actions (owner: Frontend)
  - Unit tests & basic e2e tests (owner: Frontend)
- Acceptance criteria: UI matches design; events emitted with correct payloads; feature flag toggles behavior.

4) Story: Backend instrumentation & event pipeline (3–5 pts)
- Description: Ensure events are captured in analytics pipeline and available to Data team.
- Subtasks:
  - Define event schema and contract (owner: Data/Backend) — AC: events documented and agreed.
  - Implement server-side event capture if required (owner: Backend)
  - Add experiment assignment logging server-side if relevant (owner: Backend)
- Acceptance criteria: Events appear in analytics workspace within 1–2 minutes, validated by Data.

5) Story: Experiment flagging & rollout config (2–3 pts)
- Description: Configure experiment flags and randomization rules.
- Subtasks:
  - Create experiment config in feature-flag system (owner: Eng/Platform)
  - Implement 50/50 randomization and strand allocation (owner: Eng)
  - Add kill switch for immediate pause (owner: Eng)
- Acceptance criteria: Flags tested in staging; kill switch verified.

6) Story: Analytics dashboard & alerting (3–5 pts)
- Description: Build lightweight dashboard for daily monitoring with conversion funnel and variant comparison; set alerts.
- Subtasks:
  - Create dashboard (owner: Data) — funnel: signup → displayed → activation within 7d
  - Add daily variant balance and conversion chart
  - Set alert thresholds (owner: Data/Ops)
- Acceptance criteria: Dashboard accessible to stakeholders; test data validated.

7) Story: QA & staging rollout (2–3 pts)
- Description: Full QA on staging and internal canary release.
- Subtasks:
  - End-to-end QA test (owner: QA) — AC: no console errors; events fire as expected
  - Internal pilot with team (owner: Product) — AC: at least 10 internal users tested
- Acceptance criteria: QA sign-off, no blocking bugs.

8) Story: Production rollout & monitoring (2 pts)
- Description: Launch experiment to 50/50 split; monitor daily.
- Subtasks:
  - Launch experiment (owner: Eng/Product)
  - Daily monitoring checks (owner: Data/Product for first 7 business days)
- Acceptance criteria: Balanced cohort; no safety alerts.

9) Story: Post-experiment analysis & decision (3–5 pts)
- Description: Run final analysis, prepare impact deck and recommendation (rollout, iterate, or kill).
- Subtasks:
  - Analyze primary & secondary metrics (owner: Data/Product)
  - Prepare 1–2 slide impact summary + full analysis notebook (owner: Product)
  - Present findings to stakeholders and decide next steps (owner: Product)
- Acceptance criteria: Deck delivered; decision recorded.

10) Story: Communication & CS playbook (1–2 pts)
- Description: Prep support messaging, update onboarding docs if rolling out.
- Subtasks:
  - Draft support FAQ + CS note (owner: CS/Product)
  - Update onboarding docs (owner: Docs/Product)
- Acceptance criteria: CS briefed; docs updated.

Suggested Jira fields and labels
- Component: frontend, backend, analytics, design, qa
- Labels: experiment, onboarding, activation, cohort
- Priority: High (experiment is a 90-day priority)
- Epic link: CORE-ONBOARD-A/B

Ticket title templates
- [EPIC] Onboarding Checklist A/B Test — Activation Experiment
- FEAT: Implement onboarding checklist modal (treatment)
- DATA: Instrument onboarding_checklist_displayed & activation_event
- OPS: Configure experiment flag AND kill switch
- ANALYTICS: Dashboard for onboarding experiment
- QA: Test onboarding experiment flows (staging)
- DOCS: CS FAQ + onboarding docs update

Acceptance criteria examples (copy-paste)
- FEAT: UI component emits onboarding_checklist_displayed with payload {user_id, account_id, experiment_id, variant, displayed_ts} and activation_event fires with activation_type and timestamp when user completes core action.
- ANALYTICS: Dashboard displays proper variant counts and 7-day activation conversion; data validated by comparing raw event counts to dashboard numbers (within 1–2%).
- QA: No JS errors in console; modal behaves correctly on common browsers; keyboard accessible; mobile/responsive validated.

PR checklist (for engineers)
- Feature flag present and defaults to control
- Events instrumented and schema documented
- Unit & integration tests included
- Accessibility checks done
- QA ticket linked
- Rollout & rollback instructions included in the PR description

Monitoring & safety rules (operational)
- If day-over-day variant imbalance >10% for 3 days, investigate and halt if not correctable.
- If treatment causes >5% absolute drop in activation for any important segment or critical errors > threshold, pause experiment immediately, notify stakeholders, and revert.
- Daily stand-up owner: Product + Data for first 7 days after launch.

Quick stakeholder announcement templates
- Slack message (to Eng/Design/Data/CS channels)
  - “Heads up — launching Onboarding Checklist A/B test on [start date]. Goal: +activation within 7 days. Product: [you]. Data: [owner]. Eng: [owner]. Please monitor dashboard (link) and reach out if you see anomalies. Kill-switch is [owner].”
- Email to Execs/Manager
  - Short summary, timeline, success metric, and ask to review the final analysis.

Next steps I’ll do after you send baselines
- Compute exact sample size and recommended minimum cohort size and test duration to detect your target relative uplift.
- Populate the experiment doc with baseline numbers, exact success thresholds, and pre-registered analysis (regression tests, p-value thresholds, adjustments for multiple tests if any).
- Optionally, I can draft the exact Jira tickets (full descriptions) in the format your team uses so you can paste them into Jira.

Anything else to include in the tickets (e.g., story point scale you use, sprint cadence, preferred assignees)? If not, send the baseline activation / retention / MAU and I’ll return the final sample size and a completed experiment doc within a couple hours.

messages.content:
Congrats again — Senior Product Manager is huge. Below is a practical, ready-to-use 30-60-90 plan plus a prioritized list of quick wins you can pick from to start demonstrating impact right away. I can tailor this to your product type (SaaS, consumer app, mobile, B2B platform, etc.) if you tell me a bit about it.

High-level objectives for the first 90 days
- Build credibility and trust with the team and stakeholders.
- Establish clarity on product health, priorities, and metrics.
- Deliver early, visible value and set up repeatable processes for product discovery and delivery.

30-day: Learn, stabilize, and make small wins
Goals
- Understand the product, customers, metrics, and team dynamics.
- Build relationships and a stakeholder map.
- Identify 2–3 immediate areas for improvement.

Key activities / deliverables
- Meet 1:1 with direct reports, engineering lead, design lead, data/analytics, sales, customer success, support, and key stakeholders (first 2 weeks).
- Audit product health: top 5 KPIs, active experiments, tech debt, top bugs, backlog health.
- Run a backlog triage session and identify top candidate for an immediate fix or improvement.
- Create a living 30-60-90 doc and stakeholder map; share with manager.
- Deliverable: Product Health Snapshot (dashboard + short memo with risks/opportunities).
- Deliverable: Quick-win plan for one high-impact, low-effort item.

Success metrics (examples)
- Completed 8–12 1:1s and stakeholder interviews.
- Product Health Snapshot delivered and reviewed with manager.
- One quick win implemented and measured (e.g., bug fixed, funnel step improved).

60-day: Set direction, align team, and start experiments
Goals
- Define/align on product priorities and a roadmap draft.
- Improve discovery and delivery cadence.
- Launch small experiments and refine prioritization.

Key activities / deliverables
- Run a strategy and prioritization workshop with PMs, Eng, Design, and key stakeholders.
- Finalize top 3–5 priorities for the next 3–6 months, with clear success criteria.
- Set or refine metrics/OKRs for your area.
- Implement or improve analytics events and dashboards to measure outcomes.
- Start 1–3 experiments or pilot features tied to the top priorities.
- Establish regular sync cadence (weekly PM/Eng standup, monthly stakeholder review).
- Deliverable: Draft Roadmap (90–180 day) with success metrics and owners.
- Deliverable: Experiment plan(s) with hypotheses, metrics, and timeline.

Success metrics (examples)
- Roadmap and OKRs agreed with stakeholders.
- Analytics coverage for primary funnel/metrics increased to desired level.
- At least one experiment launched with baseline measurement.

90-day: Deliver impact, iterate, and scale processes
Goals
- Deliver first meaningful outcomes from roadmap/experiments.
- Institutionalize processes: discovery, prioritization, release, and stakeholder comms.
- Create a plan for medium-term improvements (hiring, tooling, cross-functional alignment).

Key activities / deliverables
- Ship a measurable improvement or launch MVP tied to your priorities.
- Review experiment results and decide to iterate/scale/stop.
- Implement retros and continuous improvement for delivery (release process, definition of done).
- Present 90-day review to stakeholders and execs: wins, learnings, roadmap next steps.
- Create hiring or resource plan if gaps exist.
- Deliverable: 90-day review presentation + updated 6-month roadmap.

Success metrics (examples)
- Quantifiable improvement in at least one KPI (activation, conversion, retention, NPS).
- Stakeholder satisfaction (survey or qualitative feedback) improved.
- Clear, repeatable process documented and adopted by team.

Prioritized quick wins (low effort → immediate impact)
- Clear the top 1–3 production bugs impacting key flows (very high impact, low effort).
- Fix the highest-friction signup/onboarding step (improves activation quickly).
- Add or clean up critical analytics events (gives visibility to make better decisions).
- Create a single-page Product Health Dashboard and share weekly.
- Run 5–10 customer support or sales shadowing sessions to surface top pain points.
- Run a “bug bash” or UX audit and prioritize fixes for next sprint.
- Update pricing or trial messaging on the site/app if it’s clearly misleading or confusing.
- Triage backlog and remove or consolidate stale tickets (reduces noise).
- Implement a one-paragraph product update to stakeholders every 2 weeks.
- Host a quick cross-functional prioritization workshop (15–30 min) to agree top sprint focus.
- Surface a small UX tweak (copy change, CTA color, microcopy) with A/B test potential.
- Improve release checklist to reduce hotfixes / rollbacks.

Which of these are the highest priority depends on your product and company stage. If you want a quick decision rubric: prioritize items that affect conversion/retention or remove blockers for engineers (reduce cycle time, reduce urgent bugs).

Templates / tools I can provide
- A filled 30-60-90 template customized to your product.
- A ready-to-send team announcement for your promotion and top priorities.
- A one-page Product Health Snapshot template (metrics + quick actions).
- A prioritization matrix (RICE or impact/effort) prefilled with your top tickets if you share them.

Next steps
- Tell me what kind of product/company you’re at (SaaS/B2B, consumer app, marketplace, size of team).
- Which 1–2 quick wins sound best to you right now and I’ll draft an action checklist and sample communications (e.g., Slack blurb, stakeholder email, sprint ticket text).

messages.content:
Huge congrats again — love the energy! Below is a ready-to-share 30-60-90 plan tailored to a mid-market B2B SaaS with a ~6-person product/engineering team, plus a concise team announcement and concrete action checklists for the two quick wins you asked to prioritize: (1) fix top onboarding friction and (2) ship a one-page Product Health Dashboard.

Shareable 30-60-90 (one-page summary)
- Role owner: You (Senior Product Manager). Core partners: Eng Lead, Designer/UX, Data/Analytics (or whoever owns analytics), Customer Success/Sales, QA.
- High-level objectives (first 90 days)
  1. Build credibility, align stakeholders, and set measurable priorities.
  2. Remove top onboarding friction to improve activation/trial conversion.
  3. Deliver a one-page Product Health Dashboard to enable data-driven decisions.
  4. Establish repeatable discovery → delivery cadence.

30 days — Learn, stabilize, deliver one quick win
- Goals
  - Complete stakeholder and team alignment.
  - Audit onboarding funnel and current analytics.
  - Deliver Product Health Dashboard MVP (internal one-pager).
  - Implement immediate fix(es) to highest-impact onboarding friction.
- Key activities / deliverables
  - 1:1s: 8–12 meetings (Eng Lead, 2 engineers, Designer, CS, Sales, Data, Support, Exec).
  - Onboarding audit: map funnel (signup → activation → first-success) and list top 5 friction points (data + qualitative).
  - Dashboard MVP: one-page dashboard with 6–8 core metrics (see checklist below).
  - Quick onboarding fix implemented (copy/flow/bug/few-lines-of-code experiment).
  - Deliverables: Product Health Snapshot (MVP), Onboarding Audit memo, one small shipped fix.
- Success metrics
  - 8–12 stakeholder interviews complete.
  - Dashboard MVP available and shared.
  - One measurable improvement in onboarding metric (e.g., +X% onboarding completion or -Y% time-to-first-value).

60 days — Align, run experiments, and iterate

  - Deliverables: Draft 90-day roadmap, experiment plans, dashboard v1.1.

  - Experiment(s) launched with baseline tracking.

90 days — Deliver outcomes and scale processes
- Goals
  - Validate/scale winning onboarding changes.

  - Present 90-day review to execs with results and next steps.
- Key activities / deliverables
  - Ship iterative onboarding improvements based on experiment outcomes.
  - Set dashboard cadence (weekly snapshot + monthly review).

  - Deliverables: 90-day review slide deck, updated 6-month roadmap, hiring/resource needs if required.
- Success metrics
  - Quantified improvement in activation/trial conversion or time-to-first-value.

Short team announcement (Slack/email)
Hi team — I’m excited to share that I’m stepping into the Senior Product Manager role! I’m really grateful for the support and thrilled to keep building with you. For my first priority: I’ll focus on (1) removing our top onboarding friction to improve trial → activation and (2) shipping a concise Product Health Dashboard so we make faster, data-informed decisions. I’ll be scheduling short 1:1s over the next two weeks to learn from each of you and will share the 30/60/90 plan and dashboard MVP by end of week 2. If you have immediate onboarding pain points or dashboard requests, please drop them in #product-now or DM me. Excited to get started — let’s do this!

Action checklist — Quick win #1: Fix top onboarding friction
Goal: Improve the critical conversion step(s) in the onboarding funnel (e.g., trial → activation or time-to-first-value).

1) Discovery (days 0–5)
  - Owner: You (PM)
  - Tasks:
    - Pull current funnel metrics (signup → activation → paid) and baseline numbers.
    - Identify top 3 drop-off steps with numbers and qualitative evidence (support tickets, session replays, CS feedback).
    - Run 5–10 customer support / sales shadowing sessions or listen to recorded demos for onboarding pain.
  - Deliverable: One-page Onboarding Audit (top drop-offs, hypothesized causes, severity).

2) Hypothesis & prioritization (days 3–7)
  - Owner: You + Designer + Eng Lead + CS
  - Tasks:
    - For each top friction, write a short hypothesis (If we X, then Y will improve by Z%).
    - Score by impact/effort (quick wins = high impact / low effort).
  - Deliverable: Prioritized list of 1–3 experiments/fixes.

3) Implement quick fix / experiment (days 7–21)
  - Owner: Eng lead for build, Designer for UX, PM for specs, Data for instrumentation
  - Tasks:
    - Create a small scoped ticket with acceptance criteria and measurement plan (A/B or pre/post).
    - Instrument events needed (track step completion, time-to-first-value).
    - Deploy change (copy, flow tweak, bug fix, CTA change, prefilled form).
  - Deliverable: Deployed change and tracking in place.

4) Measure & decide (days 21–30)
  - Owner: PM + Data
  - Tasks:
    - Monitor experiment for minimum sample/time window.
    - Analyze impact on conversion, time-to-first-value, and downstream revenue signals.
    - Decide to iterate/scale/rollback.
  - Deliverable: Experiment result memo and next steps.

Suggested success metrics
  - +X percentage points in onboarding completion (pick realistic target e.g., +5–15%).
  - Reduced time-to-first-value (e.g., -20–40%).
  - Fewer support tickets related to onboarding (count decrease).

Example Jira/Asana ticket template for an onboarding fix
  - Title: [Onboarding] Fix: <short description>
  - Background: link to Onboarding Audit
  - Hypothesis: If we do X, then Y will change by Z
  - Acceptance criteria: measurable change + instrumented events
  - Owner(s): Eng, Design, Data
  - Est. effort: 1–3 days
  - Rollout plan: percent rollout or A/B
  - Measurement window: 2–4 weeks

Action checklist — Quick win #2: Ship one-page Product Health Dashboard
Goal: Deliver a single, regularly-updated dashboard that provides the team and stakeholders the core metrics to make decisions.

1) Define metrics & audience (days 0–3)
  - Owner: You + Data + Eng Lead
  - Core recommended metrics for a mid-market B2B SaaS one-pager:
    - Activation/Onboarding conversion rate (trial → active)
    - Trial-to-paid conversion rate (14/30-day)
    - MRR / ARR (net new & churned)
    - Churn rate (logo and revenue)
    - NPS or CSAT trend (if available)
    - Top funnel metrics (signups/leads) and demo/booked rate (if applicable)
    - Product usage signal(s): DAU/WAU/MAU for product-critical feature(s) or retention at day 7/30
    - Support/incident metric: number of critical bugs or high-severity tickets (week)
  - Audience: PM/Eng/CS weekly sync, Exec monthly.

2) Data mapping & access (days 3–7)
  - Owner: Data
  - Tasks:
    - Confirm event names & sources, ensure instrumentation coverage for onboarding events.
    - Build SQL/queries or dashboards in chosen tool (Looker/Metabase/Mode/Tableau/Grafana).
    - Establish refresh cadence (real-time vs daily).
  - Deliverable: Data queries and single-source definitions doc.

3) Build MVP dashboard (days 7–14)
  - Owner: Data + PM (UX for layout)
  - Tasks:
    - Create a clean one-page layout: top-line health, 2 quick insights, callouts for risks.
    - Add small written context: last update, owner, interpretation notes, actions recommended.
    - Add filters for key segments (account size, cohort, product line).
  - Deliverable: Dashboard v1 with share link.

4) Rollout & adoption (days 14–30)
  - Owner: PM
  - Tasks:
    - Share in team channels + include in weekly standup agenda.
    - Ask stakeholders to confirm values/definitions and provide feedback.
    - Schedule a 15–30 minute walkthrough demo for the team.
  - Deliverable: Adopted dashboard with weekly snapshot email or pinned link.

Suggested success metrics for the dashboard
  - Dashboard viewed X times/week by the team (set target e.g., viewed in >75% of weekly standups).
  - Time to access core KPI reduced (e.g., decision made in same meeting instead of follow-up).
  - Fewer ad-hoc metric requests to Data (indicates capture of common needs).

Dependencies & risks (callouts)
- Need access to analytics tool, event instrumentation, and product data warehouse.
- Quick onboarding fixes depend on engineering bandwidth—prioritize highest-impact low-effort items.
- Dashboard accuracy depends on clean event definitions; expect 1–2 iteration cycles to reconcile numbers.

Next steps (what I can do for you immediately)
- Draft a formatted shareable Google Doc/Confluence page of the 30-60-90 and the onboarding audit template.
- Draft 2 sample Jira tickets: (a) onboarding quick fix, (b) dashboard build ticket with data queries.
- If you share: current funnel numbers, analytics tool (Mixpanel/Amplitude/GA/Looker/Metabase), and top onboarding complaint(s), I’ll prefill the Onboarding Audit and a prioritized experiment list.

Love this — I can feel the buzz. Below are the prefilled Onboarding Audit, a mock one-page Product Health Dashboard (layout, core metrics, and example BigQuery/Mixpanel query skeletons), and two ready-to-create Jira tickets (Onboarding quick fix + Dashboard build). You can copy/paste these into Confluence/Jira or tell me where to format them.

1) One-page Onboarding Audit (prefilled)
Summary
- Context: Mid-market B2B SaaS. Analytics: Mixpanel + BigQuery. Current funnel (baseline): ~1,200 signups/mo, ~300 trials/mo, trial→activation 18%, trial→paid (30d) 8%, median time-to-first-value 4 days. Top qualitative pain: confusing setup flow and unclear default settings.
- Goal: Raise onboarding completion/activation and reduce time-to-first-value. Suggested short-term target: +4–6 percentage points in activation (e.g., 18% → ~22–24%) and reduce median time-to-first-value from 4 → 2–3 days.

Top funnel drop-offs (numbers + severity)
- Signup → Trial start: ~1,200 → 300 (trial conversion ~25% of signups). Severity: medium. Evidence: Mixpanel signup & trial_started events.
- Trial → Activation (first-success): trial→activation = 18% (major leak). Severity: high. Evidence: Mixpanel funnel counts, CS tickets reporting setup stuck.
- Trial → Paid (30d): 8% (needs improvement). Severity: medium-high. Evidence: billing/stripe integration events + revenue reports.

Hypothesized root causes (mapped to evidence)
1. Confusing setup flow (high severity) — users abandon during multi-step configuration; session replays & support transcripts mention unexpected steps and buried settings.
2. Unclear default settings (high severity) — users don't know recommended defaults, misconfigure and don’t get to first-success.
3. Insufficient inline guidance / contextual help (medium) — no checklist or clear next-step CTA; leads to delayed time-to-first-value.
4. Missing instrumentation for intermediate steps (medium) — can’t fully measure where users drop off within setup.

Priority quick fixes (recommended order)
1. Small-scope setup simplification + default-setting change (high impact, low effort). Example: hide optional advanced step from initial path + set recommended defaults and a short tooltip. Instrument changes.
2. Add a “Setup Checklist” and single CTA to reach first-success (medium effort). Shows progress; reduces friction.
3. Improve copy for CTAs and error guidance (low effort). Replace ambiguous labels with “Get started — recommended”.
4. Add analytics events for each setup step & detailed properties (if missing) (medium effort) — to enable future fine-grained experiments.
5. Run A/B or percent rollout of the simplified flow and measure conversion/time-to-first-value.

Recommended immediate KPI targets for the experiment
- Activation conversion: +4–6 pp (18% → 22–24%) in the experiment cohort.
- Time-to-first-value: reduce median from 4 → 2–3 days.
- Support tickets referencing setup: reduce by ~20–40% in the following month.

Next steps (days 0–7)
- Lock 1 small change scoped to a single sprint: hide advanced step + set recommended defaults + add tooltip + instrument events.
- Implement ticket, rollout to 10–20% (if possible), measure, iterate.

2) Mock one-page Product Health Dashboard (layout + core metrics)
Top row — Overview (single-line KPIs; big numbers)
- MRR / ARR (net new & churned) — show current MRR and delta last 30d
- Trials / month: 300
- Trial → Activation: 18% (baseline)
- Trial → Paid (30d): 8%
- Median time-to-first-value: 4 days
- Active critical incidents (week): 0–X

Middle row — Funnels & conversion
- Signup → Trial → Activation → Paid funnel visualization (bar/stage with counts & conversion pps)
- Time-to-first-value distribution (box or histogram)
- Cohort retention for new trials (day 7 / day 30 retention)

Bottom row — Signals & qualitative
- Top onboarding drop-off steps (ordered list + counts)
- Top 3 support ticket themes (from CS)
- Recent deploys / incidents affecting onboarding (flag)

Right column / context panel
- Last update: date/time, owner: Product (you)
- Quick insights: 1–2 lines (e.g., “Activation down 2pp vs last week; suspected setup flow confusion”)
- Action items: current experiments and owners

Suggested visuals
- KPI numbers with delta arrows
- Funnel stacked bars
- Time-to-first-value histogram
- Line chart: MRR & churn trend
- Table: Top accounts at-risk (if available)

3) Example event definitions & BigQuery/Mixpanel query skeletons
Assumptions: Mixpanel events exported to BigQuery in table events.mixpanel_events with columns: event_name, distinct_id (user_id), event_time (timestamp), properties (JSON), project, etc. Adjust names to your actual schema.

A) Monthly signups and trials (simple signup/trial events)

  COUNTIF(event_name = 'Trial Started') AS trials_month
FROM `your_project.events.mixpanel_events`

B) Trial → Activation conversion (count unique users with activation event within 30d of trial)
SQL skeleton:
WITH trials AS (

  FROM `your_project.events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY distinct_id
),
activation AS (

  FROM trials t

)

D) Median time-to-first-value

WITH first_values AS (

    TIMESTAMP_DIFF(MIN(e.event_time), t.trial_ts, DAY) AS days_to_first_value
  FROM (

    FROM `your_project.events.mixpanel_events`
    WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started' AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    GROUP BY distinct_id

    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'First Success'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY t.distinct_id, t.trial_ts
)
SELECT APPROX_QUANTILES(days_to_first_value, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_days
FROM first_values;

1) Onboarding Audit (paste into a Google Doc / Confluence page)

Title: Onboarding Audit — Quick-win plan

- Trial → Activation (First Success): 18% (major leak). Severity: high.

1. Confusing multi-step setup flow — session replays & CS reports users stuck mid-setup. (high)
2. Unclear default settings — users misconfigure and do not reach first-success. (high)
3. Insufficient inline guidance / no clear checklist leading to delays. (medium)

Measurement & validation

- Measurement window: 2–4 weeks post-rollout for statistically meaningful signal.

Notes / assumptions
- Queries and metrics rely on these Mixpanel events exported to BigQuery: "Signup", "Trial Started", "First Success", "Subscription Created". For in-flow steps we assume either "Onboarding Step Completed" or similar event is (or will be) instrumented. If names differ, update SQL accordingly.

2) BigQuery SQL (copy/paste; update project.dataset.table if needed)

Assumptions:
- Table: `events.mixpanel_events` (if your dataset/project differ, replace the full path below).
- Columns: event_name (STRING), distinct_id (STRING) as user id, event_time (TIMESTAMP), properties (JSON/STRING) containing keys like plan, account_size, setting_name. If properties are stored in STRUCT/RECORD change JSON_EXTRACT usage accordingly.
- Time windows: queries default to the last 30 days; adjust INTERVAL as needed.

A) Signups and Trials (last 30 days)
SQL:
SELECT
  COUNTIF(event_name = 'Signup') AS signups_last_30d,
  COUNTIF(event_name = 'Trial Started') AS trials_last_30d
FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP();

B) Trial → Activation conversion rate (trial start cohort, activation within 30 days)
SQL:
WITH trials AS (
  SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
  FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY distinct_id
),
activations AS (
  SELECT t.distinct_id
  FROM trials t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'First Success'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS trials_started,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activations) AS activations,
  SAFE_DIVIDE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activations), COUNT(*)) AS activation_rate
FROM trials;

C) Trial → Paid (Subscription Created within 30 days)
SQL:
WITH trials AS (
  SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
  FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY distinct_id
),
subscriptions AS (
  SELECT t.distinct_id
  FROM trials t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'Subscription Created'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS trials_started,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions) AS subscriptions_created,
  SAFE_DIVIDE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions), COUNT(*)) AS trial_to_paid_30d
FROM trials;

D) Median time-to-first-value (days) for trials with First Success within 30d
SQL:
WITH trial_first AS (
  SELECT
    t.distinct_id,
    t.trial_ts,
    MIN(e.event_time) AS first_success_ts
  FROM (
    SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
    FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
    WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
      AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    GROUP BY distinct_id
  ) t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'First Success'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY t.distinct_id, t.trial_ts
),
durations AS (
  SELECT
    distinct_id,
    TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_success_ts, trial_ts, SECOND) / 86400.0 AS days_to_first_value
  FROM trial_first
)
SELECT
  APPROX_QUANTILES(days_to_first_value, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_days_to_first_value
FROM durations;

E) Funnel counts (signup → trial → activation → paid) for last 30 days
SQL:
WITH signups AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT distinct_id
  FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Signup'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
),
trials AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT distinct_id
  FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
),
activations AS (
  -- activation tied to trial within 30 days
  SELECT DISTINCT t.distinct_id
  FROM (
    SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
    FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
    WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
      AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    GROUP BY distinct_id
  ) t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'First Success'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
),
payments AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.distinct_id
  FROM (
    SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
    FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
    WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
      AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    GROUP BY distinct_id
  ) t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'Subscription Created'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signups) AS signups_30d,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials) AS trials_30d,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activations) AS activations_30d,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments) AS paid_30d,
  SAFE_DIVIDE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signups)) AS signup_to_trial_rate,
  SAFE_DIVIDE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activations), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials)) AS trial_to_activation_rate,
  SAFE_DIVIDE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trials)) AS trial_to_paid_rate;

F) Time-to-first-value distribution (histogram buckets, last 30 days)
SQL:
WITH first_values AS (
  SELECT
    t.distinct_id,
    TIMESTAMP_DIFF(MIN(e.event_time), t.trial_ts, DAY) AS days_to_first_value
  FROM (
    SELECT distinct_id, MIN(event_time) AS trial_ts
    FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
    WHERE event_name = 'Trial Started'
      AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    GROUP BY distinct_id
  ) t
  JOIN `events.mixpanel_events` e
    ON e.distinct_id = t.distinct_id
   AND e.event_name = 'First Success'
   AND e.event_time BETWEEN t.trial_ts AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(t.trial_ts, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY t.distinct_id, t.trial_ts
)
SELECT
  days_to_first_value,
  COUNT(*) AS users
FROM first_values
GROUP BY days_to_first_value
ORDER BY days_to_first_value;

G) Top onboarding drop-off steps (requires Onboarding Step Completed event with property step_name / step_index)
SQL (if you have Onboarding Step Completed event):
WITH step_reaches AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(properties, '$.step_name'), JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(properties, '$.step_index')) AS step_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT distinct_id) AS users_reached
  FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Onboarding Step Completed'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY step_name
)
SELECT
  step_name,
  users_reached
FROM step_reaches
ORDER BY users_reached DESC;

H) Count of Settings Changed events (to detect default application)
SQL:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS settings_changes_last_30d,
  JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(properties, '$.setting_name') AS setting_name,
  JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(properties, '$.old_value') AS old_value,
  JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(properties, '$.new_value') AS new_value
FROM `events.mixpanel_events`
WHERE event_name = 'Settings Changed'
  AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY setting_name, old_value, new_value
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 50;

Notes & next steps for SQL:
- If properties are stored as RECORD / STRUCT (not JSON string), replace JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(...) with properties.setting_name or the correct path.
- If the Onboarding step event is named differently in your Mixpanel schema, update event_name accordingly.

I’d love a tailored 30/60/90-day plan and talking points for my first team meeting; I’m most excited to shape strategy and culture and most daunted by delegating effectively as responsibilities ramp up.

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Congrats again — this is exciting. Below is a focused, actionable 30/60/90 plan tailored to a Senior Product Manager leading a 7-person cross‑functional team, plus a ready-to-use first-team meeting agenda and talking points, and concrete delegation tools you can start using right away.

30/60/90-day plan (objectives, actions, success signals)

30 days — Learn, build trust, diagnose
- Objectives
  - Understand product, customers, metrics, team skills and dynamics.
  - Establish relationships and basic rhythms.
  - Identify 1–2 quick wins to build credibility.
- Key actions
  - 1:1s with each team member (60m): current work, blockers, goals, preferred communication.
  - Meet key stakeholders (engineering lead, design lead, data, sales, CS, marketing, PM peers, exec sponsor).
  - Review product metrics, roadmap, backlog, OKRs, recent retros, customer feedback and incident post-mortems.
  - Run a team kickoff (first-team meeting below).
  - Create a stakeholder map and decision-rights draft.
  - Pick one quick win (e.g., backlog cleanup, fix release pipeline bottleneck, simple UX improvement with impact).
  - Block weekly “strategic” time on calendar (2–4 hours).
- Success signals
  - 7 x 1:1s completed and documented.
  - Stakeholder map and decision model shared.
  - Quick win delivered or scoped and started.
  - Team has a regular meeting cadence scheduled.

60 days — Align strategy, delegate ownership, create plan
- Objectives
  - Co-create or validate near-term strategy and priorities.
  - Start shifting day-to-day execution responsibilities to the team.
  - Put structure around delivery and measurement.
- Key actions
  - Synthesize findings and present draft strategy / priorities for feedback.
  - Run workshops: roadmap prioritization, metrics/OKR setting, and ways of working.
  - Assign clear owners for major product areas, features, or experiments.
  - Establish success metrics and dashboards for top objectives.
  - Implement handoffs, design docs, PRD templates, and requirement for success criteria.
  - Start career/development conversations and identify training or mentorship needs.
- Success signals
  - Agreed 90-day roadmap and owner assignments.
  - Dashboards for top metrics live.
  - Team members own features/EPICs and run status with stakeholders.
  - Fewer tactical questions routed to you — team escalates appropriately.

90 days — Deliver outcomes, scale leadership, embed autonomy
- Objectives
  - Deliver measurable outcomes tied to the strategy.
  - Ensure team autonomy and scalable processes.
  - Create a continuous feedback loop for improvement.
- Key actions
  - Launch/measure primary initiatives; iterate based on data.
  - Finalize role responsibilities and delegation boundaries.
  - Document ways of working, meeting cadence, and decision frameworks.
  - Conduct a “how are we doing” team retrospective and stakeholder feedback session.
  - Set next quarter OKRs and growth plans for each team member.
- Success signals
  - Measurable improvement in one or more product metrics (conversion, retention, cycle time, feature adoption).
  - Team satisfaction and clear ownership indicators.
  - Stakeholder confidence (positive feedback; fewer escalations).
  - Clear hiring/resource plan or backlog triage in place.

First team meeting — agenda and ready-to-use script
- Suggested agenda (60 minutes)
  - 0–5 min: Quick intro + thank you
  - 5–15 min: Your background & leadership approach (concise)
  - 15–25 min: Vision & priorities (what you aim to achieve with the team)
  - 25–35 min: Ways of working (meetings, communication, decision rights, delegation approach)
  - 35–45 min: Immediate focus & quick wins (next 30 days)
  - 45–55 min: What I need from you / requests (1:1 scheduling, candid feedback)
  - 55–60 min: Q&A + next steps

- Sample opening script (short)
  - “Thanks, everyone — I’m really excited to be here. I want to start by saying I know you’ve been driving a lot of hard work already, and my first priority is to learn from you and remove blockers so we can move faster together.”
- Sample vision & priorities script
  - “Over the next quarter my goal is to ensure we focus on X (customer outcome), Y (business outcome), and Z (operational health). I’ll be looking to you to own product areas and to bring data and customer insight into our decisions.”
- Ways of working / delegation script
  - “I believe in clear ownership and autonomy. I’ll set clear outcomes and success criteria, and you’ll have authority to decide how we get there. I’ll check in at agreed cadences and be available for escalation. If anything needs quicker alignment, flag me early.”
- Immediate asks of the team
  - Schedule 1:1s this week, share current roadmaps, flag top 3 blockers, nominate an owner for each product area if not already assigned.
- Closing
  - “I want candid feedback — what’s working, what’s not, and where do you think we should start. I’ll synthesize what I hear and share a 30-day plan.”

Delegation toolkit — practical steps and templates
- Delegation ladder (use to calibrate autonomy)
  - Tell -> Sell -> Consult -> Agree -> Advise -> Inquire -> Delegate
  - Explicitly state which level you expect for a given decision.
- Quick delegation checklist (share when assigning any area)
  - Desired outcome and success metrics (acceptance criteria)
  - Decision authority (what they can decide without asking)
  - Constraints and non-negotiables
  - Timeline and milestones
  - Resources & stakeholders
  - Check-in cadence and escalation path
- Example delegation note
  - “Ownership: Checkout optimization EPIC. Outcome: +5% conversion in 8 weeks. Authority: prioritize experiments under $X cost. Check-ins: weekly 15m update. Escalation: raise risk if projected <2% improvement after 4 weeks.”
- How to let go
  - Start with low-risk tasks, increase scope as competence and trust grow.
  - Use structured check-ins rather than ad-hoc micromanaging.
  - Provide feedback after each milestone: praise specifics + one area to improve.
  - Document decisions so the team can reference why things were chosen.

1:1 question template (use during first meetings)
- What are you working on and what’s going well?
- Biggest blockers or risks?
- What are you most proud of recently?
- Where do you want to grow this year?
- How do you prefer to receive feedback and how often?
- What would help you be more effective?
- What should I know about your working style or context?

Quick wins examples (pick 1–2 in first 30 days)
- Clean up and prioritize backlog: remove stale items, add acceptance criteria.
- Ship a small UX tweak informed by top customer feedback.
- Improve deployment or QA process to reduce lead time.
- Run a focused experiment to validate a risky assumption.

Metrics and signals to track
- Product/business: activation, retention, conversion, revenue impact
- Delivery: cycle time, PR lead time, bug rate
- Team: pulse survey score, meeting effectiveness, number of owned initiatives
- Stakeholder: NPS of stakeholders or qualitative feedback

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Overloaded with tactical work -> Mitigate: protect strategy time, delegate explicitly.
- Risk: Unclear decision rights -> Mitigate: publish decision framework and stakeholder map.
- Risk: Team not bought into changes -> Mitigate: co-create priorities, communicate rationale, quick wins.

If you want, I can:
- Build a slide deck for your first team meeting using this script.
- Produce a fillable 30/60/90-day Word or Notion template with checklists.
- Draft 1:1 email templates to schedule meetings and gather pre-1:1 input.

Which of those would be most helpful next? Or tell me one key product priority and I’ll tailor the plan to that context.

  - Speaker note: Encourage one-pager feedback after meeting and how to submit.

# make_presentation.py
# Requires: pip install python-pptx Pillow
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_PARAGRAPH_ALIGNMENT
from PIL import Image
import os
from datetime import datetime

# CONFIG — edit as needed
OUTPUT_PPTX = "Growth_Product_Team_Kickoff.pptx"
TEAM_NAME = "Growth Product Team"
PRESENTER = "[Your Name] — Senior Product Manager"
DATE = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
PRIMARY_BLUE = (0x00, 0x52, 0xCC)  # #0052CC
CHARCOAL = (0x1F, 0x29, 0x37)      # #1F2937
LOGO_PATH = ""  # e.g., "company_logo.png" or leave blank to skip
MEETING_LENGTH = "60 minutes"

prs = Presentation()
blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank slide

def add_title_slide():
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
    left = Inches(0.6)
    top = Inches(1.0)
    width = Inches(7.0)
    # Title textbox
    title_box = s.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, Inches(1.2))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = f"Team Kickoff — {PRESENTER}"
    p.font.size = Pt(32)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*PRIMARY_BLUE)
    # Subtitle
    sub = s.shapes.add_textbox(left, top+Inches(1.2), width, Inches(0.6))
    stf = sub.text_frame
    sp = stf.paragraphs[0]
    sp.text = "First 30 days: learn • align • deliver"
    sp.font.size = Pt(18)
    sp.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*CHARCOAL)
    # Footer with team and date
    footer = s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(6.9), Inches(8.5), Inches(0.4))
    ft = footer.text_frame
    fp = ft.paragraphs[0]
    fp.text = f"{TEAM_NAME} • {DATE}"
    fp.font.size = Pt(10)
    fp.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*CHARCOAL)
    # Optional logo
    if LOGO_PATH and os.path.exists(LOGO_PATH):
        try:
            # place logo on top-right
            im = Image.open(LOGO_PATH)
            im_w, im_h = im.size
            aspect = im_h / im_w
            logo_width = Inches(1.6)
            logo_height = Inches(logo_width * aspect)
            s.shapes.add_picture(LOGO_PATH, Inches(8.0) - logo_width, Inches(0.3), width=logo_width, height=logo_height)
        except Exception as e:
            print("Logo addition failed:", e)

    # Speaker notes
    notes = s.notes_slide.notes_text_frame
    notes.text = ("Speaker notes:\n"
                  "Quick thank-you and 1–2 sentence excitement opener: "
                  "“Thanks everyone — I’m thrilled to be here. I want to start by recognizing the hard work I’ve already seen "
                  "and say my first priority is to learn from you and remove blockers so we can move faster together.”")

def add_content_slide(title, bullets, notes_text):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
    # Title
    title_box = s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.6), Inches(8.5), Inches(0.8))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(24)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*PRIMARY_BLUE)
    # Bullets
    body = s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(1.6), Inches(8.5), Inches(4.2))
    btf = body.text_frame
    btf.word_wrap = True
    for i, b in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = btf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = b
        else:
            p = btf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = b
        p.level = 0
        p.font.size = Pt(16)
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*CHARCOAL)
    # Notes
    notes = s.notes_slide.notes_text_frame
    notes.text = "Speaker notes:\n" + notes_text

# Slides content definitions (title, bullets, speaker notes)
slides = [
    ("Agenda",
     ["Quick intro & leadership approach",
      "Vision & top priorities",
      "Ways of working & delegation",
      "Immediate focus & quick wins",
      "Requests & next steps",
      "Q&A"],
     "Run through agenda; share a short 30-day plan and leave time for questions."),
    ("Quick intro",
     [f"Short background: [2-sentence: prior role, relevant achievement]",
      "Human note: [1-line personal]",
      "First priority: Learn & remove blockers"],
     "2–3 sentences about your background; emphasize humility and eagerness to learn."),
    ("How I work",

      "Clear ownership: defined decision rights and accountability",
      "Data + customer-informed: experiments and customer insight",
      "Psychological safety: candid feedback and learning from failure"],

    ("Top priorities (This quarter)",
     ["Customer outcome: Improve activation for new users",
      "Business outcome: Increase conversion by [X%] / revenue signal [Y]",
      "Operational health: Reduce cycle time; improve predictability"],
     "Explain why each matters, invite the team to help refine numeric targets."),
    ("Meetings & purpose",
     ["Weekly standup (15m) — sync on blockers",
      "Weekly product sync (30–45m) — planning & priorities",
      "Monthly stakeholder review — progress to ops/sales/execs",
      "1:1s (60m first; then 30m ongoing)"],
     "Clarify attendees and success criteria for each meeting."),
    ("Delegation Ladder — how decisions will be made",

      "Inquire — “Tell me your plan; I’ll ask clarifying q’s.” (High autonomy)",
      "Advise — “You propose; I’ll give recommendations.” (Medium-high)",
      "Agree — “We co-create the decision.” (Shared)",
      "Consult — “Talk to impacted parties and come back.” (Medium)",
      "Sell — “I’ve decided; I’ll get your buy-in.” (Low autonomy)",
      "Tell — “I decide and you execute.” (Direct)"],
     "When assigning, I’ll state the ladder level. Example: 'Delegate — own checkout funnel, run experiments to hit X metric.'"),
    ("Delegation checklist",
     ["Outcome & success metrics (what winning looks like)",
      "Decision authority (what you can decide)",
      "Constraints & non-negotiables",
      "Timeline & milestones",
      "Resources & stakeholders",
      "Check-in cadence & escalation path"],
     "I’ll include these in assignment notes. Use the checklist to reduce back-and-forth."),
    ("First 30 days — quick wins",
     ["Backlog cleanup: remove stale items; add acceptance criteria",
      "One high-impact UX tweak driven by top feedback",
      "Deploy/QA pipeline improvement to reduce lead time"],
     "Invite volunteers to own these items now or offline this week."),
    ("How you can help",
     ["Schedule 1:1s this week (I’ll send invites)",
      "Share roadmaps & top 3 blockers",
      "Be candid: feedback & ideas welcomed",
      "Champion ownership and clarity"],
     "Explain preferred format for blockers (Slack channel or shared doc) and timelines for 1:1s."),

]

add_title_slide()
for title, bullets, notes_text in slides:
    add_content_slide(title, bullets, notes_text)

prs.save(OUTPUT_PPTX)
print("Saved:", OUTPUT_PPTX)
print("If you want the PPTX to include a logo, set LOGO_PATH to a PNG/JPG file and run again.")

  - Implement a defect‑reduction initiative: mandatory RCA for P1s, bug triage cadence, test coverage targets for critical paths.
  - Introduce or tighten CI/CD guardrails (merge criteria, automated tests gating deploys).
- Team & engagement
  - Set individual development goals with each report and identify growth/mentorship plans.
  - Start a recognition ritual (weekly shoutouts + “wins” note) and a monthly team retro action list.
- Measure & communicate
  - Track early metrics from Phoenix (deployment success rate, customer-impacting bugs).
  - Deliverable at day 60: 60‑day progress report showing Phoenix status, initial KPI deltas, and proposed 90‑day initiatives.

61–90 days — Scale wins, formalize roadmap, and lock KPIs
- Measure & optimize
  - Review time‑to‑market and defect metrics vs baselines; quantify progress toward your 20%/30% targets and iterate.
  - If Phoenix had issues, complete RCAs and feed changes into the roadmap.
- Scale successful practices
  - Roll out proven CI/CD/test automation improvements across teams.
  - Formalize release & dev playbooks and an incident post‑mortem process.
- Org & retention
  - Propose role adjustments/hiring and career ladders where needed.
  - Run a formal engagement pulse survey; act on top 2 improvement areas.
- Deliverables (end of 90 days)
  - 90‑day review with VP Eng: KPI trends, Phoenix outcomes, 6–12 month roadmap, resourcing requests, and a proposed org/process improvements list.

- Weekly: Phoenix stand (while active), team standups, dashboard check.
- Biweekly: 1:1s, sprint review, stakeholder sync.
- Monthly: KPI dashboard (lead time, deployment frequency, escaped defects, eNPS/turnover).
- Definitions to track: lead time for changes, cycle time, escaped defects (production bugs/1000 LOC or per release), deployment success rate, voluntary turnover rate, team eNPS.

2) 30/60/90-day plan (practical, organized by goal, actions, milestones, and metrics)

Overview: First 30 = listen & assess; 60 = align & plan; 90 = execute & measure.

Days 1–30: Learn, build trust, identify quick wins
- Goals: Understand team dynamics, stakeholders, product health; build credibility.
- Key actions:
  - 1:1s with direct reports (30–60 min) to learn responsibilities, pain points, career goals.
  - 1:1s with key stakeholders: engineering, design, sales, customer success, marketing, analytics, leadership.

  - A prioritized short list of quick wins shared with team
- Success metrics:
  - 100% of direct reports met
  - Baseline metrics captured
  - At least one quick win scoped and started

Days 31–60: Align vision, refine roadmap, improve processes
- Goals: Build alignment around priorities, refine roadmap, set success metrics.
- Key actions:
  - Host a working roadmap session with cross-functional leads to align on priorities and constraints.
  - Define/iterate on KPIs and success criteria for top initiatives.
  - Create or improve processes: sprint planning, PRD template, decision log, release checklist.
  - Start delegating ownership and set clear expectations/OKRs for direct reports.
  - Kick off 1–2 medium-sized initiatives (from quick-win momentum) with clear owners.
- Milestones:
  - Shared and signed-off 90-day roadmap and success metrics
  - Documented team responsibilities and decision processes
  - First sprint delivered under any new process improvements
- Success metrics:
  - Stakeholder alignment (written or meeting consensus)
  - Roadmap with prioritized initiatives and measurable outcomes

Days 61–90: Execute, measure results, iterate
- Goals: Demonstrate progress on roadmap, embed metrics-driven habits, scale team capabilities.
- Key actions:
  - Monitor progress on key initiatives, run weekly check-ins and unblock issues.
  - Launch the first measurable feature/initiative and collect data/feedback.
  - Retrospective on processes: what’s working, what to adjust.
  - Plan hiring or reallocation if capacity gaps are identified.
  - Set longer-term product strategy and OKRs for next quarter.
- Milestones:
  - Successful delivery/launch of a prioritized initiative with measurement plan
  - Quarterly OKRs and roadmap for next cycle
  - Hiring plan or role adjustments documented
- Success metrics:
  - Improvement on target KPIs (e.g., activation, retention, revenue lift, reduced cycle time)
  - Stakeholder satisfaction and team confidence in roadmap

- Weekly 1:1s with direct reports (30–45 min)
- Weekly product sync with engineering & design (30–60 min)
- Biweekly stakeholder demo / roadmap sync
- Monthly leadership update (written + short sync)

- Improve onboarding microcopy or first-time user flow to lift activation
- Run a 2-week customer interview blitz for high-usage segments

5) Risks & mitigations
- Risk: moving too fast without stakeholder buy-in — Mitigation: early alignment sessions and written decisions
- Risk: spreading yourself too thin — Mitigation: delegate ownership, focus on highest-impact objectives
- Risk: insufficient data to prioritize — Mitigation: instrument tracking for critical funnels immediately

30–60–90 day plan (for Senior Product Manager, team of 8; start May 15)
High-level aim: learn the product & team, align priorities with stakeholders, and deliver measurable early wins that create momentum.

Days 1–30 (May 15–June 14) — Learn & stabilize
- Purpose: build relationships, map current state, surface risks and quick wins.
- Key outcomes:
  - One-on-ones completed with all 8 direct reports and primary cross-functional partners.
  - Inventory of active projects, backlog health, roadmap, metrics, and tech/UX debt.
  - 1–2 scoped quick wins with owners.
- Activities:
  - Schedule 30–45 min 1:1s with each direct report in first 10 business days.
  - Meet 45–60 min with key partners: Eng lead, Design lead, Data/Analytics, QA, Sales/CS, Marketing, and Product Ops.
  - Review product analytics (DAU/MAU, activation, conversion funnels), current OKRs, roadmap, recent sprint/release notes, customer feedback/tickets.
  - Quick audit: backlog prioritization, cycle time, release cadence, outstanding P0/P1 bugs.
  - Identify low-effort/high-impact improvements (examples below).
- Success metrics:
  - 8 direct 1:1s + top 5 stakeholder meetings completed.
  - Clear list of top 6 priorities and top 6 risks.
  - Quick win(s) scoped with owner and timeline.
- Quick-win examples for PM:
  - Fix a high-impact P0/P1 bug or UX friction affecting conversion.
  - Publish a prioritized backlog and freeze scope for the next sprint.
  - Add/clean an analytics event to measure a key activation step.
  - Re-run and summarize NPS/CSAT feedback for last quarter.
- Risks & mitigations:
  - Data gaps — request analytics/dashboard access immediately.
  - Competing priorities — get manager alignment on top-3 objectives for first 90 days.

Days 31–60 (June 15–July 14) — Align & plan
- Purpose: propose direction, get team buy-in, and kickstart quick wins.
- Key outcomes:
  - Team-approved 90-day plan and top 3–5 objectives (with KPIs).
  - Owners assigned and timelines for major initiatives.
  - First quick-win milestone delivered.
- Activities:
  - Present observations & proposed priorities to your manager and stakeholders; incorporate feedback.
  - Run a team workshop to align on goals, decision rights, and success metrics.
  - Establish cadences: weekly standups, sprint reviews, roadmap reviews, monthly exec updates.
  - Start or unblock work on quick wins.
- Success metrics:
  - Team sign-off on priorities.
  - One quick-win completed or at a measurable milestone.
  - Owners assigned to primary initiatives with timelines.
- Example KPIs to track:
  - Activation conversion %, feature adoption %, time-to-ship (cycle time), sprint velocity stability, bug count P0–P2, customer satisfaction/CSAT.

Days 61–90 (July 15–Aug 13) — Execute & scale
- Purpose: deliver measurable progress, refine processes, and start people development.
- Key outcomes:
  - Clear movement on at least one leading KPI (e.g., +X% activation).
  - Reliable team processes (backlog grooming, release process) and defined metrics dashboard.
  - Development plans started for directs.
- Activities:
  - Drive execution, remove blockers, and escalate when needed.
  - Implement or refine dashboards and reporting to leadership.
  - Run retrospectives and incorporate improvements.
  - Begin 1:1 development conversations and career planning.
- Success metrics:
  - Tangible improvement on targeted KPI(s).
  - Consistent sprint/release cadence and owners documented.
  - Development goals defined for each direct.

One-on-one agenda — direct reports (30–45 min)
- Structure:
  - 3 min: quick check-in (energy, context).
  - 5 min: role & priorities confirmation (what they own right now).
  - 12–15 min: current work deep-dive (top 2–3 projects, status, blockers, dependencies).
  - 8–10 min: wins + pain points + ideas (what’s working, what to change).
  - 5 min: development & expectations (career goals, stretch opportunities, what they need from you).
  - 2–3 min: agree next steps and follow-up.
- Starter questions (pick 3–4):
  - What are the top outcomes you’re measured on this quarter?
  - What’s the single biggest blocker slowing you down today?
  - Which product decision are you worried will be made without enough data?
  - If you could change one process to make your work 20% faster, what would it be?
  - Where do you want to grow in the next 6–12 months?
- Cadence recommendation: weekly for first 8–12 weeks, then move to biweekly as relationships and rhythms stabilize.
- Quick follow-up note template (1–3 bullets):
  - Thanks — summary of 2–3 takeaways, owners, and next steps. (Send within 24 hours.)

One-on-one with cross-functional partners (30–60 min)
- Topics to cover:
  - Mutual goals and how our teams measure success.
  - Handoffs, decision rights, and escalation paths.
  - Current dependencies, risks, and what each side needs in the next 30 days.
  - Communication preferences and meeting cadences.
- Outcomes: clear contact owner list, agreement on handoffs, and any immediate asks documented.

Kickoff email (short, use on day 1 — May 15)
Subject options:
- “Hi team — excited to join as Senior Product Manager (May 15)”
- “Hello from your new Senior Product Manager — 1:1s & next steps”

If there’s anything urgent I should know about (major risks, blockers, upcoming deadlines), please reply or flag it to me directly. My initial focus will be understanding our roadmap, metrics, and areas for quick impact (bugs/UX, analytics gaps, and backlog health).

Looking forward to meeting everyone and hearing about what’s working and where we can improve.

Best,
[Your name]
Senior Product Manager

Anything else I can draft for you?

Below are a ready-to-send announcement (short + slightly longer), a focused 30/60/90-day plan you can adapt, and practical one-on-one tips to establish credibility fast. Tell me if you want it tailored to your org size, product stage (launch/growth/mature), or specific stakeholders.

Announcement — short (Slack/email headline)
- I’m excited to share that I’ve stepped into the Senior Product Manager role. I’m grateful for the team’s support and looking forward to partnering across teams to drive customer value and deliver on our priorities. Happy to chat 1:1 — ping me anytime!

Announcement — slightly longer (team/all-hands)
- I’m thrilled to announce that I’ve accepted the Senior Product Manager role. Thank you to everyone who’s supported me — I’m energized to continue working with this team to deepen customer focus, accelerate key outcomes, and improve how we ship. Over the next weeks I’ll be listening, learning, and aligning priorities; please reach out if you have feedback or want to sync on product direction. Excited for what’s ahead!

30/60/90-day plan (concise, actionable)
- Goal: Build credibility, align stakeholders, and deliver early, measurable value.

First 30 days — Listen & Learn
- Objectives: Understand product, customers, team dynamics, metrics, and stakeholders.
- Key actions:
  - Meet 1:1 with direct reports, PM peers, engineering lead, design, sales/CS, and your manager (30–45 min each).
  - Review key product metrics, roadmap, backlog, customer feedback, and major initiatives.
  - Sit in on support/triage calls or customer interviews.
  - Map stakeholders, decision rights, and current priorities.
- Success metrics:
  - Completed 1:1s with top ~10 stakeholders.
  - Clear list of top 3 customer pains and top 3 technical/operational risks.
  - Draft prioritized opportunities list.

Days 31–60 — Align & Prioritize
- Objectives: Set priorities, pick 1–2 early wins, and align roadmap with stakeholders.
- Key actions:
  - Run a prioritization workshop (RICE/MoSCoW or simple impact/effort) with PM/eng/design.
  - Define 1–2 quick-win experiments or improvements (e.g., funnel optimization, UX fix, onboarding flow).
  - Create/communicate a 3–6 month roadmap draft and proposed metrics.
  - Establish regular cadences (weekly PM sync, monthly stakeholder review).
- Success metrics:
  - Agreed top priorities and roadmap shared.
  - One quick-win scoped and in development or experiment running.
  - Stakeholder alignment rating (informal check) improved vs Day 0.

Days 61–90 — Deliver & Iterate
- Objectives: Deliver initial wins, measure impact, and institutionalize processes.
- Key actions:
  - Launch quick wins / experiments; define success criteria and measurement.
  - Refine roadmap based on learnings and feedback; set OKRs/KPIs for next quarter.
  - Improve handoffs (product <> eng <> design) — establish clear definition of ready/done.
  - Publicize results and learnings to stakeholders.
- Success metrics:
  - At least one measurable improvement shipped (e.g., +X% conversion, -Y% onboarding time).
  - Roadmap and OKRs approved or endorsed by manager/stakeholders.
  - Documented process improvements (e.g., meeting cadence, PRD template).

One-on-one tips to build credibility fast
- Cadence & length:
  - Direct reports: weekly or biweekly 30–45 min. Skip if unnecessary but keep a regular cadence.
  - Peers/stakeholders: 30–60 min monthly or as needed.
- Agenda template (quick and repeatable):
  - Quick check-in (1–2 min) — personal/energy level.
  - Top priorities/blockers since last sync (5–10 min).
  - What they need from you (5–10 min) — decisions, resources, escalation.
  - Feedback and career/trajectory talk (5–10 min for direct reports).
  - Recap + next steps (1–2 min).
- Questions to ask early (to learn & build trust):
  - What’s going well? What’s blocking you?
  - What would you improve about how we build/ship?
  - What do customers/users say we should focus on?
  - How do you prefer to receive feedback/decisions?
  - What are your goals and how can I help?
- Behaviors that build credibility:
  - Listen first, summarize to confirm you understood, then act.
  - Be decisive and transparent: explain trade-offs and rationale.
  - Own mistakes and communicate learnings quickly.
  - Deliver on small promises (quick wins) consistently.
  - Surface data + customer context when asking for alignment.
- Follow-up habits:
  - Send a 1–2 line recap and explicit next steps after each 1:1.
  - Track commitments and deliver on them; if delayed, proactively update.
  - Use shared docs for visibility (notes, decisions, action items).

Want this tailored?

  - Run 1–3 growth experiments (A/B tests, onboarding tweaks, email drips, re-engagement).
  - Work with engineering to prioritize platform stability/perf fixes affecting growth funnels.
  - Define and socialize 3-month roadmap and growth KPIs; set OKRs draft for next quarter.
  - Establish regular reporting cadence: weekly metrics sync and experiment reviews.
  - Coordinate with marketing to amplify proven wins (campaigns, paid channels).
- Deliverables / success signals:
  - At least one live experiment; early results tracked and analyzed.
  - Stakeholder alignment on top priorities and responsibilities.
  - Reduced cycle time for shipping small experiments (measureable process improvement).

Days 61–90 — Iterate, measure impact & scale
- Objectives:
  - Validate winners, scale successful experiments, and institutionalize growth processes.
- Key actions:
  - Analyze experiment outcomes, roll out successful changes to production, and iterate on lossy experiments.
  - Finalize OKRs and a quarter roadmap informed by data.
  - Create playbooks for repeatable growth tactics (onboarding optimization, retention campaigns).
  - Improve handoffs: PRD/templates, definition-of-ready/done, and experiment tagging for analytics.
  - Communicate wins and learnings broadly.
- Deliverables / success signals:

  - Documented experiment/playbook library and established growth cadence.
  - Roadmap & OKRs signed off by your manager and key stakeholders.

Example quick-win ideas for a growth-stage product

- Email reactivation drip for dormant users.
- Improve conversion on top funnel landing pages or pricing page.
- Reduce friction in checkout/payment or core task flow.

C. First-week 1:1 schedule (practical calendar-ready plan)

Principles

- Keep a mix of short intro meetings and a few longer deep dives.

Ready-to-use 30-60-90 plan (customizable)

Principles: early listening + data, align with stakeholders, deliver visible value, create repeatable processes.

0–30 days — Learn & Align (goal: understand product, people, metrics, and top opportunities)
- Objectives
  - Build relationships with manager, PM peers, engineering leads, design, data, sales/CS, and marketing.
  - Audit product and metrics to identify top pain points and opportunities.
  - Understand roadmap, OKRs, release cadence, and decision framework.
- Actions
  - 1:1s: schedule 30–60 minute one-on-ones with 8–12 key stakeholders; use a short template (see script below).
  - Review analytics: funnels, activation, retention, top feature usage, revenue-impacting flows.
  - Read docs: PRDs, postmortems, backlog, roadmaps, customer research.
  - Sit with support/CS for a day or review top N support tickets.
  - Map the product ecosystem and dependencies.
- Success measures
  - Documented stakeholder map and their top priorities.
  - List of 5–8 hypotheses/opportunities with estimated impact and effort.
  - Baseline dashboard for key metrics.

30–60 days — Prioritize & Prototype (goal: define priorities and run early experiments)
- Objectives
  - Align on top priorities and get buy-in for 1–2 quick experiments or improvements.
  - Define clear success metrics for each chosen initiative.
  - Start executing on low-risk, high-impact work.
- Actions
  - Run a prioritization session (RICE/ICE/Value vs Effort) with stakeholders for top 10 initiatives.
  - Define MVP/experiment designs and success criteria for chosen initiatives.
  - Launch 1–2 experiments (A/B test, UX tweak, pricing experiment, onboarding flow).
  - Improve processes: introduce a lightweight product meeting cadence (roadmap review, weekly sync).
- Success measures
  - Prioritized roadmap for next 3–6 months with stakeholder buy-in.
  - At least one experiment launched and collecting data.
  - Clear decision-making rubric and communication cadence.

60–90 days — Deliver & Scale (goal: show measurable impact and stabilize roadmap)
- Objectives
  - Deliver first validated outcomes and secure resources for scaling.
  - Institutionalize improvements and handoffs.
  - Set long-term roadmap and metrics for success.
- Actions
  - Analyze experiment results; iterate or scale winners.
  - Ship a small, high-visibility improvement or milestone (feature release, onboarding revamp, retention campaign).
  - Present results and proposed roadmap to leadership.
  - Identify hiring or tooling needs and create a 6–12 month plan.
- Success measures
  - At least one measurable improvement in a key metric (e.g., activation +10%, churn -X% or conversion uplift).
  - Roadmap and resourcing plan approved by manager/stakeholders.
  - Repeatable process for prioritization, discovery, and releases.

Quick wins (pick 3–5 to pursue in the first 30–60 days)
1. Top support ticket triage — identify the 3–5 most common/high-impact bugs or UX issues and get them fixed. Time to value: 1–3 weeks. Impact: immediate reduction in friction/CS load.
2. One small onboarding UX A/B test — test a headline, CTA, or reduce steps in signup. Time to value: 2–6 weeks. Impact: activation/conversion lift.
3. “Customer insights” lightning report — synthesize top themes from recent N customer interviews/support logs and present to the team. Time: 1 week. Impact: aligns team on top pain points.
4. Quick cohort analysis — run a retention/churn cohort for latest 3 releases to find where users drop off. Time: 1–2 weeks. Impact: reveals highest-leverage fixes.
5. Ship a low-effort high-impact feature or tweak — e.g., surface most-used feature faster, fix slow-loading page, or add a tiny automation. Time: 2–6 weeks. Impact: visible product improvement.
6. Establish a weekly engineering–product design sync to unblock work and speed delivery. Time: immediate. Impact: faster resolutions and fewer surprises.
7. Create a one-page decision framework (how we prioritize, what counts as success). Time: 1 week. Impact: reduces conflict and speeds decisions.

How to pick quick wins
- Prioritize: low effort + high impact + high visibility.
- Show one “fast” win (quick fix), one “data” win (insight-driven experiment), and one “relationship” win (stakeholder alignment).

Love this — congrats again. Below is a tailored 30–60–90 plan for a Senior PM at a B2B SaaS productivity tool in growth/scaling, plus three prioritized quick wins mapped to activation, 30-day retention, and MRR.

High-level focus areas
- Reduce friction in activation to increase conversion from trial/onboarded users → paying users.
- Improve early retention (30-day) by rescuing drop-off points and increasing value realization.
- Increase MRR by improving trial→paid conversion and expansion motions for power users.

30 days — Learn, baseline, and align (goal: deep context + a clear hypothesis backlog)
- Objectives
  - Build relationships and align priorities with engineering, design, data, sales, and CS.
  - Establish baselines for activation, 30-day retention cohorts, and MRR (trial→paid and expansion).
  - Surface top friction points from data + voice of customer.
- Actions
  - 1:1s: 30–45m with manager + key leads; share a short agenda (their top priorities, pain points, expectations, preferred comms).
  - Audit analytics: recent cohorts (last 3 months), conversion funnel from signup → activation → trial completion → paid; top event drop-offs.
  - Read product docs, backlog, current experiments, support/CS ticket themes, and recent win/loss notes from sales.
  - Create a one-page stakeholder map and a prioritized hypothesis list (impact vs effort).
  - Stand up a simple dashboard (daily/weekly) for activation, 7/30-day retention, trial→paid conversion, MRR delta.
- Success measures / deliverables
  - Baseline dashboard and cohort report.
  - 5–8 prioritized hypotheses/opportunities with RICE/ICE scoring.
  - Calendar of quick stakeholder syncs and decision cadence.

30–60 days — Experiment & prioritize (goal: launch 1–2 measurable experiments and align roadmap)
- Objectives
  - Run prioritized experiments aimed at activation and early retention.
  - Define a short roadmap for the next 3 months tying experiments to MRR impact.
  - Tighten handoffs with Sales/CS for trial conversion and expansion.
- Actions
  - Select top 2 experiments (one activation, one retention/MRR) using RICE.
  - Write lean experiment specs (hypothesis, metric, sample, length, rollout plan, rollback criteria).
  - Implement in-app messaging/onboarding flows and email sequences with design/engineering.
  - Coordinate with Sales to implement trial qualification triggers and a playbook for high-value trials.
  - Weekly review of experiment telemetry with data and eng/design.
- Success measures / deliverables
  - At least one experiment live and collecting statistically meaningful data.
  - Prioritized 3-month roadmap and resource asks.
  - Draft sales/CS playbook for top trial/expansion scenarios.

60–90 days — Validate, scale, and institutionalize (goal: ship validated improvements and prepare to scale winners)
- Objectives
  - Analyze and iterate on experiment results; scale winners into roadmap.
  - Improve processes for continuous discovery, prioritization, and measurement.
  - Present outcomes and ask for resources/hiring if needed.
- Actions
  - Run final analysis, prepare a results presentation tying changes to activation/30d retention/MRR impact.
  - If experiments succeed, prioritize engineering tickets to fully productize the change.
  - Institutionalize reporting cadence (weekly dashboard, monthly stakeholder review).
  - Identify tooling/hiring needs (e.g., product analytics, growth PM, UX researcher).
- Success measures / deliverables
  - At least one measurable improvement (example targets below).
  - Roadmap + resourcing plan approved.
  - A repeatable experiment/launch process documented.

Suggested metric targets (example goals to discuss with manager)
- Activation rate +8–15% over baseline in 90 days (depending on current numbers).
- 30-day retention lift +3–7 percentage points (small improvements compound to big revenue wins).
- MRR uplift: +3–8% attributable to trial→paid conversion and early expansion plays (benchmarks vary by business).

Three prioritized quick wins (pick all 3 in parallel if you can staff them)

1) Onboarding / Activation A/B test (Highest priority for activation)
- Why: Activation typically has the largest immediate impact on trial→paid conversion.
- Hypothesis example: “If we reduce time-to-first-success by adding a 3-step guided setup with checklists and an inline sample/template, activation will increase by X%.”
- Steps
  - Define “activation” event (e.g., user completes key action that correlates with retention).
  - Design two variants: current vs streamlined guided flow or new CTA/feature placement.
  - Instrument metrics (primary: activation rate within first 7 days; secondary: 30-day retention, NPS).
  - Run for defined sample size (or duration) and measure.
- Time to value: 2–6 weeks.
- Owners: PM + Design + Eng + Data.
- Success metric: statistically significant lift in activation; target +8–12% depending on baseline.

2) 30-day retention cohort & targeted drip/reactivation play
- Why: Early churn is a big driver of MRR loss; targeted nudges and education can rescue users.
- Steps
  - Run cohort analysis to identify when and which segments drop off (role, company size, use case, onboarding steps not completed).
  - Develop 2–3 targeted flows: in-app nudges for users stuck on a step, contextual help, and a 7–21 day email education series for new users.
  - Create a high-touch CS/Sales outreach list for high-value trials showing early churn signals.
  - Measure lift in 30-day retention for cohorts receiving the intervention vs control.
- Time to value: 2–4 weeks for cohort + flows; 4–8 weeks to see retention delta.
- Owners: PM + Data + CS + Design.
- Success metric: +3–7pp lift in 30-day retention for targeted cohorts.

3) Quick MRR win: Trial→Paid funnel optimization + expansion trigger
- Why: Small changes in conversion and early expansion compound MRR quickly.
- Steps
  - Audit trial to paid conversion funnel: trial length, friction points in billing/upgrade, Sales handoff, trial qualification criteria.
  - Implement one quick change: clearer price/benefit messaging on trial end screen, simplified billing flow, or in-app upsell microcopy for power users.
  - Add a usage-based expansion trigger (e.g., when a team hits X active seats or Y completed tasks, prompt upgrade with a tailored CTA + trial-to-paid sales follow-up).
  - Track conversion rate and MRR per cohort.
- Time to value: 2–6 weeks.
- Owners: PM + Sales + Data + Eng.
- Success metric: +5–10% trial→paid conversion for targeted experiments; measurable MRR lift for cohorts.

Quick operational tips
- Define activation and success metrics before any change; pre-register analysis plan.
- Run experiments on segments that represent meaningful MRR (don’t waste Sales time on low-value trials).
- Use an experiment rubric (min detectable effect, sample size, cadence) to avoid false positives.
- Communicate early wins in the first 60 days to build momentum and trust.

Dashboards / queries to establish first
- Funnel: signup → key activation event → trial completion → paid conversion (by cohort).
- Retention cohorts (day 7/30/90) segmented by acquisition channel, company size, onboarding completion.
- MRR by cohort, new vs expansion MRR, churn by cohort.
- Top support ticket themes correlated to funnel drops.
